I can share what I know about the 2011-12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team, though I should note my information may have gaps or inaccuracies, so verify important details.

**Overview:**
The 2011-12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team had a historic season under head coach Tommy Amaker. It was a landmark year for the program.

**Key Achievements:**
- The team won the Ivy League championship (sharing or winning outright with Penn — I believe they shared the regular season title with Penn but won the playoff)
- They earned Harvard's first NCAA Tournament appearance in 66 years (since 1946)
- The team achieved a national ranking in the AP Top 25 for the first time in program history, climbing as high as around #21-25 at various points

**Notable Players:**
- Keith Wright - a key frontcourt player and previous Ivy League Player of the Year
- Oliver McNally - senior guard, team leader
- Brandyn Curry - point guard
- Kyle Casey - forward
- Laurent Rivard - shooter
- Christian Webster

**Coach:**
Tommy Amaker, who had taken over the program in 2007, continued building Harvard into an Ivy League power.

**NCAA Tournament:**
Harvard received a 12-seed (I believe) and faced Vanderbilt in the first round, losing the game. This ended their historic season.

**Significance:**
This season was a major turning point for Harvard basketball, transforming it from a historically modest program into a consistent Ivy League contender. It set the stage for further NCAA Tournament appearances in subsequent years.

I'd recommend checking sources like Harvard Athletics or sports references for exact statistics, the final record, and tournament details, as I may have some specifics wrong.
